name: The High household at 2021 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_high_mrs_james_l

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2021 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2021 Mrs. James L. High & dr..

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2021, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. It lists no live-in staff at the house on 1 June 1900. Left off: J. L. High (written "at Lakeside", with an office address; nobody else is listed at the house). The 1910 census (T624 roll 241, ED 166 and 167) was read for this card's children: the children it lists, and those the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911, are on the card with the years each lived here, whether or not they were at home in 1904. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.

persons.name: Shirley T. High

born.note: The 1910 census gives age 36 on 15 April 1910, so born about 1873-1874.

persons.note: Listed at 2021 under Mr. and Mrs. James L. High from 1897 to 1899, with his own wife in 1903, and from 1909, when he heads the house: the 1910 census lists him there with his wife Helen and their sons James and Raymond (ED 167, sheet 2A, lines 20-23). The 1904 to 1908 editions do not list him there. That they were a son of the house is read from the shared surname at the number; the Blue Book does not print the relationship.
